thread.title: These 6 Stocks Could Drag Down the Market | Investopedia

author: investopedia.com
title: These 6 Stocks Could Drag Down the Market | Investopedia
text:
Since the stock market correction in late January and early February, just six stocks have driven 42% of the subsequent rise in the S&P 500 Index (SPX) , per research by trading analytics firm INTL FCStone, as cited by Business Insider . These stocks include Google parent Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ), Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ), Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), Mastercard Inc. ( MA ), Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT ) and Visa Inc. ( V ). Their market capitalizations and gains since the correction ended on Feb. 8 are presented in the table below.
Too Risky: Six Stocks Drive 42% of S&P 500's Post-Correction Gains
Stock Market Cap Gain Since Correction Alphabet $825 billion 19.8% Amazon $963 billion 49.1% Apple $1.065 trillion 46.7% Mastercard $231 billion 38.8% Microsoft $874 billion 36.3% Visa $332 billion 32.4% Source: Yahoo Finance; based on adjusted closing price data through Sept. 27.
Why Investors Should Be Concerned History indicates that bull markets often come to an end shortly after the major stock indexes reach record highs that are marked by narrow leadership or low breadth, according to Vincent Deluard, a macro strategist at INTL FCStone. For recent examples, he points to the market collapses in 2000 and 2007, which also followed periods in which the market indexes rode to new record highs on the backs of a relatively small number of stocks. When a small number of stocks drive a disproportionate amount of the gains in the major indexes, that frequently covers up broader weaknesses in the rest of the market, Business Insider indicates.
"The next few weeks could be a perfect storm for the U.S. equity market." —Vincent Deluard, macro strategist at INTL FC Stone. Source: Business Insider
"Much of this year's action suggests a [rising interest] rate-driven correction is nearing," as Deluard stated in a recent note to clients, as Quote: d by Business Insider. The Quote: in the box above comes from the same note. Deluard believes that a "slow topping process" already is underway in the stock market, and that any combination of the following 6 factors could trigger a correction in the next few weeks.
Seasonality. Late September and early October tend to be the worst periods for stocks.
Buyback blackouts. The third quarter earnings reporting season is coming up soon, and regulations prohibit corporate share repurchases for several weeks around earning announcements. Share buybacks have been a major source of demand for stocks in this bull market, so the blackout will remove that prop to prices, at least for a time.
More difficult growth comparisons. Earnings growth in the third quarter of 2017 was in the double digits on a year-over-year (YOY) basis . Topping that in 2018 will be difficult.
Political risk. Besides the U.S. midterm elections to Congress in November, a national election in Brazil and a budget presentation in Italy are on the docket for October.
ECB tightening. In addition to the U.S. Federal Reserve , the European Central Bank (ECB) also is reversing its policy of quantitative easing (QE) that has kept interest rates down and propped up asset prices.
U.S. budget deficit. To fund the growing federal deficit, the U.S. Treasury is issuing an increasing amount of debt. This is pushing yields up, and drawing capital away from corporate stocks and bonds.
How Investors Should Respond Options traders, meanwhile, are registering more bearishness about the direction of the market than they have in 28 years, according to one indicator. This is another reason for caution. (For more, see also: Key Market Risk Measure Highest in 28 Years .)
Investors who share Deluard's bearish viewpoint should start taking defensive measures. Recently, JPMorgan offered strategies in several asset classes, geared towards protecting against a recession-induced market decline. (For more, see also: 4 Ways to Avoid Big Losses in the Next Recession: JPMorgan .)
